crop.notes: Whole item, from headline 'SULLIVAN-M'CAFFERY. Warrants for the Sluggers' Arrest Issued To-day—Local Opinion.' to Allen's last answer.

ocr.notes: Close to the image. Small slips: 'Judge Hill' prints as 'Judge Fill'; Allen 'laughed heartily', not 'openly'; 'why I don't call that a fight', not 'they don't'. The Philadelphia dateline and the 'Tom Allen' subhead are left out.

title.suggested: Allen's opinion of the Sullivan–McCaffery fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch asked Tom Kelly and Tom Allen about the Sullivan–McCaffery fight, threatened by arrest warrants in Philadelphia. Allen called McCaffery a 'newspaper wind-bag' and a coward Sullivan would knock out in one round.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Thursday, April 2, 1885', page 7. The item is in the fourth column.

facts.fact: Allen predicted that John L. Sullivan would knock out Dominick McCaffery in one round if allowed to fight to win, and dismissed McCaffery as a coward after gate money
facts.quote: Why that old newspaper wind-bag McCaffery couldn't lick anybody. Of course if they are going to stop the fight as soon as Sullivan sails in, why I don't call that a fight. But if they let Sullivan go in to win he'll knock him out in one round.

facts.fact: Asked whether McCaffery would fight Sullivan outside the city if police stopped the bout, Allen said he would not
facts.quote: No, sir; he won't. He's too big a coward and besides, that would let him out of the gate money.

notes: The arrest warrant for Sullivan and McCaffery was issued in Philadelphia, not St. Louis. It is general boxing news, so it is left out of the facts.
